diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopic Transparenchymal Nodule Access (BTPNA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Minimally invasive approach to diagnosing and treating peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs).
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Integrates imaging and precise bronchoscopic navigation to create a direct transparenchymal pathway; guided under fused fluoroscopy; performed under general anesthesia; sheath with blunt stylet for tissue sampling.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Enhances diagnostic yield while minimizing complications such as pneumothorax compared to TTNA.
limitations: technical challenges for certain lesion locations.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Particularly for nodules without a bronchus sign or not directly accessible via traditional bronchoscopy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: providing a high diagnostic yield ranging from 72.8% to 75.4%, regardless of the presence of a bronchus sign [6].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Transthoracic needle aspiration (TTNA)
limitations: Substantial pneumothorax risk of up to 15%.

diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: It boasts a biopsy yield of 86.3%, significantly outperforming guided TBNA, which only achieved a 67.2% yield [7].

diagnostic_approaches.name: VBN-guided bronchoscopic localization using liquid dyes
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Localization/positioning of pulmonary nodules to facilitate surgical resection.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Uses liquid dyes such as methylene blue, medical glue, indocyanine green, and lipiodol for positioning.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides clear visibility during surgery to aid resection.
limitations: Potential for diffusion after injection leading to imprecise localization.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For localizing peripheral pulmonary nodules preoperatively.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: VBN-guided bronchoscopic localization using liquid dyes achieves success rates between 85% and 96% [8, 9],

diagnostic_approaches.name: VBN-guided placement of spring coils
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Localization of lung nodules for surgery.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Placement of spring coils under VBN guidance; position confirmable by X-ray.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When durable localization is needed to reduce displacement risk.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: VBN-guided placement of spring coils has a success rate of 98.4% [10].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Archimedes Virtual Bronchoscopy Navigation System
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Plan BTPNA by identifying optimal airway entry and avascular path to the nodule.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Reconstructs CT into a 3D model of airways, vessels, and lung; maps POE and safe pathway.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: enabling the identification of an optimal point of entry (POE) on the airway wall and an avascular path through the lung tissue to the PPNs.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Fused fluoroscopy
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Real-time image guidance by overlaying CT-based navigation onto fluoroscopy during procedures.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Combines live fluoroscopic imaging with preoperative CT data to overlay the virtual navigation pathway.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Enhances accuracy of instrument placement and identification of critical structures.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Fused fluoroscopy, in particular, combines live fluoroscopic imaging with preoperative CT data, enabling the operator to overlay the virtual bronchoscopic navigation pathway onto the fluoroscopic image.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Enhances the ability to locate and biopsy otherwise inaccessible nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: As a navigation method for peripheral nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: such as VBN and electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB), laid the foundation for BTPNA by enhancing the ability to locate and biopsy nodules

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopic Transparenchymal Nodule Access (BTPNA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Enable targeted biopsies of peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs).
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Plan with high-resolution CT and navigation software; navigate to POE; puncture airway wall; dilate with balloon; advance sheath under fluoroscopy/navigation; perform biopsy via sheath.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Tissue obtained is used for histopathological analysis; multiple sampling techniques maximize representative sample; high diagnostic yield (especially without bronchus sign).
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When targeted biopsy of PPNs is needed.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The BTPNA procedure is a complex and meticulously planned operation designed to enable targeted biopsies of PPNs.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Preprocedural Vascular Mapping
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify critical vessels adjacent to the target lesion.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use CT imaging to map vessels near the lesion before the procedure.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Determines vessel proximity to guide an avascular access path.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Preprocedural Vascular Mapping Identification of critical vessels adjacent to the target lesion based on CT imaging.

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-based 3D Navigation Planning
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Reconstruct anatomy to select POE and an avascular path to the nodule.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain high-resolution CT; process with navigation software (e.g., Archimedes) to build a 3D model and plan an avascular path.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides a calculated, avascular pathway from POE to the nodule.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The CT data are then processed using advanced navigation software, like the Archimedes system, which reconstructs the imaging into a comprehensive three-dimensional model.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Real-time fluoroscopic or navigation guidance during sheath advancement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Maintain correct pathway and reach the nodule without deviation.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Advance sheath using real-time fluoroscopy or the navigation system.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Ensures on-course trajectory to the target nodule.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During pathway creation and sheath advancement.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: using real-time guidance from fluoroscopy or the navigation system. This ensures that the pathway remains on course

diagnostic_approaches.name: Fused fluoroscopy for lesion targeting
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm sheath position and guide biopsy at the lesion.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use fused fluoroscopy to confirm sheath location and perform biopsy.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Verification of correct sheath placement prior to sampling; fluoroscopic guidance during biopsy.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: After sheath placement and during biopsy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: confirmation of sheath position at the lesion under fused fluoroscopy, and (e) biopsy of the lesion under fused fluoroscopy guidance

diagnostic_approaches.name: Forceps biopsy through BTPNA sheath
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Obtain solid tissue samples from the nodule.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Introduce standard bronchoscopic biopsy forceps through the sheath to grasp and remove solid tissue.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides solid tissue for histopathological analysis; part of multimodal sampling to maximize representativeness.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When solid tissue sampling is required during BTPNA.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Forceps biopsy is used to grasp and remove solid tissue, while brush biopsy collects surface cells for examination.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Brush biopsy through BTPNA sheath
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Collect surface cells from the lesion.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Introduce a brush through the sheath to collect surface cells.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Cellular sampling complements forceps biopsy to improve representativeness.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When cytologic surface sampling is needed during BTPNA.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: brush biopsy collects surface cells for examination.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Needle aspiration through BTPNA sheath
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Draw fluid or small tissue samples from the lesion.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use a needle via the sheath to aspirate fluid or small tissue into a syringe.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Complements forceps and brush biopsies to increase likelihood of representative sampling.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When fluid or fine tissue aspiration is indicated during BTPNA.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Needle aspiration might also be used to draw fluid or small tissue samples into a syringe.

treatment_algorithms.title: BTPNA surgical procedure algorithm (planning, pathway setup, sampling)
treatment_algorithms.condition: Peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs) targeted with BTPNA
specific_recommendations: Initially, high-resolution CT scans of the patient’s chest are obtained.
The CT data are then processed using advanced navigation software ... which reconstructs the imaging into a comprehensive three-dimensional model.
The software’s ability to identify an avascular path from the POE to the nodule is crucial.
The patient is placed under general anesthesia to ensure comfort and immobility during the procedure.
A coring needle is then used to puncture the airway wall, creating the initial opening for the tunnel.
This opening is enlarged by the insertion of a balloon catheter, which is inflated to dilate the puncture site.
A sheath equipped with a blunt dissection stylet is carefully advanced through the lung parenchyma, using real-time guidance from fluoroscopy or the navigation system.
Through this sheath, various biopsy tools, such as forceps and brushes, are introduced to collect tissue samples from the nodule.
decision_points_and_pathways: (a) Puncture at the POE guided by navigation
(b) Balloon catheter used to dilate the tunnel
(d) Confirmation of sheath position at the lesion under fused fluoroscopy
(e) Biopsy of the lesion under fused fluoroscopy guidance
treatment_algorithms.patient_population_criteria: The BTPNA procedure is a complex and meticulously planned operation designed to enable targeted biopsies of PPNs.
monitoring_requirements: Using real-time guidance from fluoroscopy or the navigation system
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: BTPNA surgical procedure: (a) Puncture at the POE guided by navigation, (b) balloon catheter used to dilate the tunnel, (c) placement of the sheath

clinical_guidelines.title: Indications: Peripheral Pulmonary Nodule Biopsy
specific_recommendations: The primary clinical application of BTPNA lies in the diag- nosis of PPNs

integration of BTPNA with the Archimedes navigation system has yielded remarkable results, providing a high diagnostic yield ranging from 72.8% to 75.4%, regardless of the presence of a bron- chus sign
BTPNA has shown even greater efficacy for lesions without a bronchus sign that are not directly accessible via traditional bronchoscopy, achieving diagnostic yields between 71.4% and 74.1%

When com- pared to other bronchoscopic techniques, such as trans- bronchial needle aspiration and transbronchial biopsy, which have diagnostic yields of 59.1% and 22.6%, respec- tively, BTPNA has proven to be superior. It boasts a biopsy yield of 86.3%, significantly outperforming guided TBNA, which only achieved a 67.2% yield
In contrast to TTNA, which has a substantial pneumothorax risk of up to 15%, BTPNA’s bronchoscopic approach signif- icantly reduces this risk
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: PPNs; lesions without a bronchus sign
outcome_measures: diagnostic yields between 71.4% and 74.1% for lesions without a bronchus sign
guided TBNA 67.2% vs BTPNA biopsy yield 86.3%
TTNA pneumothorax risk of up to 15%
alternative_approaches: trans- bronchial needle aspiration and transbronchial biopsy
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: providing a high diagnostic yield ranging from 72.8% to 75.4%, regardless of the presence of a bron- chus sign

clinical_guidelines.title: Localization of Peripheral Pulmonary Nodules
specific_recommendations: there are currently no published reports specif- ically detailing the use of BTPNA for the localization of PPNs, this innovative technique has already been implemented in clinical practice for this purpose
VBN-guided bronchoscopic localization using liquid dyes achieves success rates between 85% and 96%
VBN-guided placement of spring coils has a success rate of 98.4%
liquid dyes such as methylene blue, medical glue, indocyanine green, and lipiodol are commonly used for positioning
Metal markers, though less commonly used for lung nodule localization, offer the benefit of remaining in place for extended periods, reducing the likelihood of displacement
outcome_measures: success rates between 85% and 96% (liquid dyes, VBN-guided)
alternative_approaches: VBN-guided bronchoscopic localization using liquid dyes

clinical_guidelines.title: Therapeutic Application: Peripheral Pulmonary Nodule Ablation
specific_recommendations: Ablation techniques such as radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation, or cryoablation can be deployed through the sheath
BTPNA-guided RFA was uti- lized to treat simulated pulmonary nodules in canines, dem- onstrating both feasibility and safety
transient inflammation and congestion, which resolved within a week, leading to the development of fibrotic scar tissue by 30 days
no long-term complications were observed
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: patients who are poor candidates for surgical resection
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Ablation techniques such as radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation, or cryoablation can be deployed through the sheath

clinical_guidelines.title: Therapeutic Application: Recanalization of Tracheal or Bronchial Obstructions
specific_recommendations: BTPNA also holds potential value in guiding the recanaliza- tion of tracheal or bronchial obstructions
By creating a tunnel in the bronchial wall, BTPNA allows for the strategic deployment of instruments for sampling or treatment

the combined use of YAG laser, cryotherapy, and balloon dilation, followed by the implanta- tion of a silicone stent, led to the successful recanalization of the occluded left main bronchus and the recovery of left atelectasis
outcome_measures: successful recanalization of the occluded left main bronchus

clinical_guidelines.title: Contraindications for BTPNA
specific_recommendations: patients who are not suitable candidates for routine bronchos- copy or general anesthesia
Patients with severe cardiovascular disease, advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or other significant comorbidities
patients with a bleeding tendency whether due to coagulopathy, use of anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications, or thrombocytopenia
Vascular wrapping, where the nodule or the pathway is encircled by significant blood vessels
proximity to critical struc- tures such as the heart, major arteries, or the esophagus
Patients with advanced pulmonary conditions, such as severe emphysema, bullae, mediastinal emphysema, or a history of pneumothorax
Lesions located at the apex of the lung are particularly problematic due to the steep angles required to reach these areas
lesions that are surrounded by blood vessels or located in regions where there is a significant angle between the bronchial tract and the lesion
alternative_approaches: alternative diagnostic or therapeutic approaches should be considered
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Patients with advanced pulmonary conditions, such as severe emphysema, bullae, mediastinal emphysema, or a history of pneumothorax

clinical_guidelines.title: Complications management in BTPNA
clinical_guidelines.condition: BTPNA-related complications (pneumothorax, hemorrhage, infection, bronchial injury)
specific_recommendations: Minor cases of pneumothorax are often managed conservatively, with close monitoring through chest X-rays.
In more severe cases of pneumothorax, the insertion of a chest tube may be required to evacuate the air and reexpand the lung.
Minor bleeding can often be controlled with local pressure or the application of hemostatic agents.
If a major blood vessel is inadvertently injured, it may lead to severe hemorrhage, requiring more aggressive interventions, such as vascular intervention or even surgical repair.
Adhering to strict aseptic techniques during the procedure.
Use of broad-spectrum antibiotics before and after the procedure can help prevent or treat infections.
Bronchial injury prevention: precise procedural techniques, including careful navigation and controlled advancement of instruments.
Bronchial injury management: conservative observation or surgical intervention if more severe.
decision_points_and_pathways: Pneumothorax: minor (monitor with chest X-rays) vs severe (insert chest tube).
Hemorrhage: minor (local pressure/hemostatic agents) vs major vessel injury (vascular intervention or surgical repair).
Bronchial injury: minor (close observation) vs more severe (surgical intervention).
monitoring_requirements: Close monitoring through chest X-rays for minor pneumothorax
Careful postprocedural monitoring for signs of infection
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Minor cases of pneumothorax are often managed conservatively, with close monitoring through chest X-rays.

clinical_guidelines.title: Prevention strategies to minimize risks during BTPNA
specific_recommendations: Comprehensive preprocedural planning, utilizing high-resolution CT scans and advanced navigation systems, is foundational for charting a precise, avascular pathway that avoids critical structures.
The expertise of the operator is equally crucial ... this proficiency significantly decreases the likelihood of procedural complications and enhances overall safety.
Selection of appropriate tools, such as the FleXNeedle for precise airway puncture and balloon catheters for safe dilation.
Continuous real-time monitoring during the procedure, using fluoroscopy and navigation systems.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Continuous real-time monitoring during the procedure, using fluoroscopy and navigation systems, allows for the early detection of any deviations, enabling immediate corrective actions

clinical_cases.content: The method, as detailed in a case report involving a 32-year-old female with pulmonary tuberculosis, leverages advanced navigation systems like the Archimedes System to create a three- dimensional model from CT scan data, facilitating precise guidance during the procedure. In this particular case, the combined use of YAG laser, cryotherapy, and balloon dilation, followed by the implantation of a silicone stent, led to the successful recanalization of the occluded left main bronchus and the recovery of left atelectasis.
